tutorial.title: Absolute Position
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to position any element to the sides of your screen.

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent: Let's learn how to position elements based on the edges of a webpage. For example, the link placed on the right edge of the webpage below.

lessons.title: Absolute
lessons.interactiveContent:
To start placing an element at a particular spot on the screen, we set position to absolute.

Make sure to pick absolute.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To start placing an element at a particular spot on the screen, we set position to absolute.

Complete the rule for the newsletter link only.

Make sure to pick a, followed by absolute.

lessons.title: Zero pixels
lessons.interactiveContent:
To put the element on the right, we use right: 0px;. This means that the element is 0px away from the right side of the page.

Make sure to pick right followed by : and then 0px, ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To put the element flush with the webpage's right side, add the side-offset declaration. Its distance must be 0px.

To put the element on the right, we use right: 0px;. This means that the element is 0px away from the right side of the page.

Make sure to pick right, followed by :, 0px, and finally ;.

lessons.title: Top zero
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use top, bottom, right, or left properties for positioning. top: 30px; sets the element exactly 30px away from the top of the page.

Make sure to pick top followed by : and then 30px, ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
For absolute positioning here, top, bottom, right and left set distances from the page edges.

Place the link 30px from the top edge, keeping it against the right edge.

Make sure to pick top, followed by :, 30px, and finally ;.

lessons.title: In flow
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's compare relative and absolute positioning. Notice how in a relative position the image is after the link?

Make sure to pick relative.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Pick the position value that keeps the link in normal flow while still letting offset properties like top move it later.

Let's compare relative and absolute positioning. Notice how in a relative position the image is after the link?

Make sure to pick relative.

lessons.title: Out of flow
lessons.interactiveContent:
Setting the link to position: absolute removes it from the normal flow and causes it to overlap the image instead.

Make sure to type absolute.

absoluterelativestatic

lessons.title: Question: Zero pixels
lessons.interactiveContent:

A link 0px from the right side of the webpageA link in its original position

A link 0px from the right side of the webpage.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The link is absolutely positioned and has right: 0px. Where is its right edge placed?

Against the webpage's right sideAgainst the webpage's left side0px below the webpage's top side

Against the webpage's right side.

lessons.title: Question: Top zero
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display?

A link 0px from the top side of the webpageA link 0px from the bottom side of the webpage

A link 0px from the top side of the webpage.
lessons.hardModeContent:
An absolutely positioned link has top: 0px. Which page edge has no space above the link?

The top edgeThe bottom edgeThe right edge

Make sure to pick The top edge.

lessons.title: Question: Out of flow
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we set an element to position: absolute;?

The element is taken out of normal flowThe element stays in normal flow

The element is taken out of normal flow.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Setting position: absolute removes an element from normal flow, so its original space is no longer reserved.

A paragraph follows an image. You make only the image absolute. What happens to the paragraph?

It can use the space that the image used to reserve.It still leaves the same space for the image.It also becomes absolutely positioned.

It can use the space that the image used to reserve.
